Recommendation
Adopt Resolution No. UT-1556 authorizing the General Manager to execute a contract,
and any necessary documents, including any amendments, with Tri-Pacific Supply, Inc.,
for the purchase of Sensus USA residential gas meters and Advanced Metering
Infrastructure (AMI) equipment, including technical and commercial support for the
products; ABB Global analytical software; Baker Hughes natural gas regulators; Kerotest
Manufacturing Corporation large insulators and insulated valves; Safeco Filter Products
Inc. commercial and industrial gas filters; and Sensit Technologies natural gas detection
instruments, in a total amount not to exceed $6,000,000 for a period of two years, with
the option to renew for one additional two-year period, at the discretion of the General
Manager.
Executive Summary
The Long Beach Public Utilities Department (LBPUD) utilizes a variety of equipment and
parts to operate and maintain the City of Long Beach’s natural gas distribution system.
Equipment and parts require regular maintenance and replacement to ensure proper
working order. To keep equipment maintained properly, and for their warranties to remain
valid, replacement OEM parts must be procured from a certified service provider. The
LBPUD uses:
• Sensus USA residential gas meters and Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI)
equipment to measure the gas consumption by volume for billing purposes;
• ABB Global (ABB) analytical software in our natural gas Supervisory Control and
Data Acquisition (SCADA) system to monitor natural gas flow and pressures;
• Baker Hughes regulators at natural gas regulator stations to maintain natural gas
distribution system pressures;
• Kerotest Manufacturing Corporation large insulators and insulated valves to
prevent cathodic corrosion and prevent natural gas leaks;
• Safeco Filter Products Inc. commercial and industrial gas filters; and
• Sensit Technologies natural gas detection instruments to locate and monitor
natural gas leaks in the field.
Tri-Pacific Supply, Inc., is the sole source provider of products and technical support
services for Sensus USA, ABB, Baker Hughes, Kerotest Manufacturing Corporation,
Safeco Filter Products Inc., and Sensit Technologies in the City of Long Beach and the
State of California. Sole source letters have been provided by the manufacturers.
BOARD OF PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSIONERS
May 14, 2026
Page 2
City Charter Section 1801 requires that contracts for LBPUD purchases be awarded to
the lowest responsible bidder after a competitive bid process, but allows for awards
without a competitive bid process when, as here, such an award is supported under the
law and authorized by a Resolution adopted by the Board.
This recommendation supports LBPUD’s FY 26 Business Plan by driving proactive
innovation within internal operations, improving efficiency, aligning resources to meet
future needs, and minimizing downtime.
Fiscal Impact
The cost to the Gas Fund will be incurred in FY 26 and FY 27, with the total amount not
to exceed the contract total of $6,000,000. These costs are included in the Gas Fund FY
26 and FY 27 Budgets and financial projections.

RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation to adopt a Resolution authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to
execute a contract, and any necessary documents including any necessary subsequent
amendments, with Motorola Solutions, Inc., of Chicago, IL, for the purchase of equipment
related to a conventional analog radio system upgrade in a total amount not to exceed
$1,172,026, for a period of two years, at the discretion of the City Manager; and,
Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute a lease-purchase agreement and
related financing documents with Banc of America Public Capital Corp, of San Francisco,
CA, for the financing of a conventional analog radio system upgrade, payable over a ten-
year period at an interest rate to be determined when the agreement is executed.
(Citywide)
DISCUSSION
City Council approval is requested to enter into a contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc. (Motorola)
for the purchase and delivery of conventional analog UHF/VHF equipment and to execute a
lease-purchase agreement through the City of Long Beach’s (City) Master Lease Agreement
with Banc of America Public Capital Corp (BAPCC), for financing of the radio system equipment.
The City operates two radio systems—analog and digital—used by various departments,
including the Police and Fire Departments. The analog system is a legacy communication
platform that relies on traditional radio waves, while the digital system (700 MHz Land Mobile
Radio System) converts voice into digital signals, providing clearer audio quality, improved
range, and enhanced modern features. Although digital radio technology is now widely adopted,
analog systems remain necessary for interoperability with external agencies that still rely on
analog communication. The City’s current analog system is over 30 years old and is no longer
supported by Motorola. Upgrading to new Motorola equipment will modernize the City's analog
radio infrastructure and reestablish long-term support and serviceability. As City departments
transition to the digital radio system, the analog system will serve as a backup, primarily for the
Fire and Police Departments and for tactical, special operations, and strategic scenarios.
This purchase is proposed without a competitive bid process because the City’s existing
Motorola portable/mobile radios can be integrated seamlessly with the modernized UHF/VHF,
creating a significant cost savings. Because the City currently uses Motorola devices, continuing
to utilize Motorola creates a streamlined transition. Motorola has agreed to offer the City the
same terms and conditions as afforded to the County of Los Angeles (L.A. County) in the
Honorable Mayor and City Council
August 12, 2025
Page 2
Motorola/L.A. County master contract (L.A. County Master Agreement) for a significant
equipment discount. The total cost, including estimated sales tax, is $1,172,026. In addition, the
City’s upgrade will allow for better interoperability with regional resources and could play an
essential role in the City’s timely response and recovery in a major disaster.
City Charter Section 1801 requires that contracts for City purchases be awarded to the lowest
responsible bidder after a competitive bid process but allows for awards without a competitive
bid process when authorized by a Resolution adopted by the City Council.
City Council approval is also requested to authorize the City Manager to execute a ten-year
lease-purchase agreement through the City’s Master Lease Agreement with BAPCC, to finance
equipment for the City’s UHF and VHF LMR system. The Master Lease Agreement was
approved by the City Council on September 18, 2018, to provide lease financing for a variety of
capital equipment purchases. The Master Lease Agreement streamlines the purchasing and
financing process to provide a cost-effective approach to facilitate the purchase of essential
capital assets. This allows the City to meet immediate service demands for maintaining the level
of annual expenditure and spreading the acquisition costs over the term of the financing rather
than budgeting a large one-time capital project expenditure.
This matter was reviewed by Deputy City Attorney Adam Jacobs on July 21, 2025, Administrative
Analyst Tommy Ryan on July 15, 2025, and by Budget Analysis Officer Greg Sorensen on July
28, 2025.
TIMING CONSIDERATIONS
City Council action to adopt a Resolution and award a contract with Motorola concurrently and
execute a lease-purchase agreement with BAPCC is requested on August 12, 2025, to ensure
the contract is in place expeditiously.
LEVINE ACT
This item is subject to the Levine Act. The Mayor, Councilmembers, and Commissioners who
have received a contribution of more than $500 within 12 months prior from a party, participant,
or their representatives involved in this proceeding may do either of the following: (1) disclose
the contribution on the record and recuse themselves from this proceeding; OR (2) return the
portion of the contribution that exceeds $500 within 30 days from the time the elected official
knew or should have known about the contribution and participate in the proceeding.
All parties, participants, and their representatives must disclose on the record of this proceeding
any contribution of more than $500 made to the Mayor or any Councilmembers within 12 months
prior to the date of the proceeding. The Mayor, Councilmembers, and Commissioners are
prohibited from accepting, soliciting, or directing a contribution of more than $500 from a party,
participant, or their representatives during a proceeding and for 12 months following the date a
final decision is rendered.

FISCAL IMPACT
The total amount of the contract will not exceed $1,172,026. The equipment purchase will be
lease-financed, paid for by the General Services Fund Group in the Technology and Innovation
Department. The annual debt service payments will be funded from the current debt service
budget from which the City’s first round of critical technology needs was previously funded. The
upgrade to the analog radio system was part of the anticipated first round spend plan. There is
sufficient appropriation in the General Services Fund Group in the Technology and Innovation
Department to cover the annual debt service payments.
Based on the indicative interest rate of 4.01 percent on July 28, 2025, the total amount for the
lease purchase with BAPCC is estimated at $1,424,611, which includes principal, interest, and
escrow fees. This equates to approximately $142,461 in annual debt service costs for the ten-
year life of the financing. The amount is subject to change and will be finalized when the
agreement is executed.
This recommendation has no staffing impact beyond the normal budgeted scope of duties and
is consistent with the existing City Council priorities. There is no local job impact associated with
this recommendation.

Approve recommendation.

RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation to adopt a Resolution authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to
execute a contract, and any necessary documents including any necessary subsequent
amendments, with Knox Associates, Inc., dba the Knox Company, of Phoenix, AZ, for
providing Knox Keysecure parts, equipment, installation services and a 5-year cloud
software license for the Long Beach Fire Department’s fire apparatus, in an amount of
$225,130, authorize a 10 percent contingency in the amount of $22,513, for a total
contract amount not to exceed $247,643, for a period of two years, with the option to
renew for three additional one-year periods, at the discretion of the City Manager.
(Citywide)
DISCUSSION
City Council approval is requested to enter into a contract with Knox Associates, Inc., dba the
Knox Company, for the purchase and installation of a new Knox Keysecure unit system to be
installed in the Long Beach Fire Department’s (LBFD’s) fleet of fire apparatus.
The KnoxBox system is a fire safety program that started in the City of Long Beach (City) in
1983. It was commenced and designed to provide fire departments and other emergency
personnel access into buildings to deliver fire mitigation or emergency medical services. The
KnoxBox system contains keys to participating properties and provides public safety personnel
access to critical facility features that support fire department operations inside of the building.
These keys include access to the fire control room, elevator keys, and other access devices for
unique infrastructure associated with buildings located throughout the City. The KnoxBox system
also allows LBFD fire prevention inspectors access to conduct annual fire inspections as
required by the California Fire Code.
KnoxBox systems are utilized as a fire service national best practice. It eliminates safety hazards
by allowing public safety personnel immediate access into a building, reducing time delays
caused by waiting for property owners or managers to respond to an emergency at a building.
The KnoxBox system protects inventory, equipment and various supplies from unnecessary
water damage caused by delayed sprinkler shut-off. For example, during sprinkler activation,
access to a KnoxBox allows fire department personnel to quickly turn off the sprinkler water flow
once the fire has been extinguished. This access prevents further water and property damage.
LBFD inspects KnoxBox devices during the annual fire inspection for buildings throughout the
City. Each box is accessed via a patented key. In addition to the parts, equipment, and
Honorable Mayor and City Council
March 4, 2025
Page 2
installation, this purchase also includes access to the KnoxConnect cloud platform system via a
5-year cloud software license, which will enhance LBFD’s ability to manage Knox devices
remotely within a single interface. Use of this system will enhance overall security of this
program.
Transitioning to the new Knox Keysecure system is the initial phase to enhance building security.
The second phase includes working with building owners throughout the City to coordinate
system and hardware upgrades. LBFD will send detailed information to building owners with
further guidance on how to work directly with the Knox Company to obtain new hardware.
Preliminarily, LBFD forecasts that most buildings can utilize existing KnoxBox units if they
proceed with a key mechanism upgrade, estimated to cost $250 through the Knox Company.
KnoxBox units that are damaged should be fully replaced with new KnoxBox hardware. Costs
for hardware will be paid by the building owner who is responsible for upgrading this type of
infrastructure.
Transitioning buildings in the City to this new system is expected to take several years. In the
meantime, businesses can continue to use the current key until the decision is made to perform
the hardware upgrade.
The Knox Company is authorized as the sole source vendor who holds patent rights and
performs the manufacturing for Knox Keysecure products. LBFD obtained a sole source
documentation letter from the Knox Company.
City Charter Section 1801 requires that contracts for City purchases be awarded to the lowest
responsible bidder after a competitive bid process but allows for awards without a competitive
bid process when accompanied by a Resolution adopted by the City Council.
This matter was reviewed by Eliezer Ben-Shmuel on February 12, 2025, and by Administrative
Analyst Tommy Ryan and Budget Development Officer Jennifer Rodriguez on January 28, 2025.
TIMING CONSIDERATIONS
City Council action to adopt a Resolution and award a contract concurrently is requested on
March 4, 2025, to ensure the contract is in place expeditiously.

This item is subject to the Levine Act. The Mayor, Councilmembers, and Commissioners who
have received a contribution of more than $500 within 12 months prior from a party, participant,
or their representatives involved in this proceeding may do either of the following: (1) disclose
the contribution on the record and recuse themselves from this proceeding; OR (2) return the
portion of the contribution that exceeds $500 within 30 days from the time the elected official
knew or should have known about the contribution and participate in the proceeding.
All parties, participants, and their representatives must disclose on the record of this
proceeding any contribution of more than $500 made to the Mayor or any Councilmembers

Commissioners are prohibited from accepting, soliciting, or directing a contribution of more

FISCAL IMPACT
The total amount of the contract for Knox Keysecure parts, equipment, installation services,
and a 5-year cloud software license will not exceed $247,643, inclusive of a 10 percent
contingency. As the cost to install the new Knox Keysecure system is unbudgeted, if approved,
LBFD will attempt to absorb the cost within its General Fund Group appropriations or find
alternative funding sources. Should it be determined that there is insufficient appropriation,
staff will evaluate one-time funds available at the end of FY 25 in the General Fund Group and
will return to City Council with a future budget adjustment. If sufficient year-end funds do not
materialize in FY 25, operating reserves may need to be utilized to cover the cost of this
system. This recommendation has no staffing impact beyond the normal budgeted scope of
duties and is consistent with existing City Council priorities. There is no local job impact
associated with this recommendation.

RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation to adopt a Resolution authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to
execute a contract, and any necessary documents including any necessary subsequent
amendments, with Kalmikov Enterprises, Inc., dba Fire Apparatus Solutions, Inc., of
Rialto, CA, for the purchase of Kovatch Mobile Equipment (KME) fire engine parts and
repair services, in an annual amount of $200,000, authorize a 10 percent contingency in
the amount of $20,000, for a total annual amount not to exceed $220,000, for a period of
two years, with the option to renew for three additional one-year periods, at the discretion
of the City Manager; and,
Increase appropriations in the Fleet Services Fund Group in the Financial Management
Department by $220,000, offset by funds available generated by the revenue received
through the Fleet Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). (Citywide)
DISCUSSION
City Council approval is requested to enter into a contract with Kalmikov Enterprises, Inc., dba
Fire Apparatus Solutions, Inc., for the purchase of Kovatch Mobile Equipment (KME) fire engine
parts and service to support the Long Beach Fire Department (LBFD).
The LBFD operates six KME fire engines in the City of Long Beach (City) that are eight years
old. The Fleet Services Bureau (Fleet), in the Department of Financial Management, maintains
and repairs these units as part of the City's fleet maintenance program. The fire engines are
maintenance-intensive and require regular service and parts to sustain daily and emergency
operations. Using original equipment manufacturer (OEM) parts ensures the vehicles and
equipment are maintained to original performance standards and factory warranty conditions are
honored. Currently, Fleet technicians provide daily inspection, parts replacement, and preventive
maintenance for the six fire engines currently in operation. Additional service assistance is
needed for breakdowns that occur more frequently in the older units.
Kalmikov Enterprises, Inc., dba Fire Apparatus Solutions, Inc., is the sole authorized distributor
of KME Fire engine parts and service in the region and is the only authorized dealer in Southern
California able to perform warranty work on the KME fire engines.
City Charter Section 1801 requires that contracts for City purchases be awarded to the lowest
responsible bidder after a competitive bid process but allows for awards without a competitive
bid process if accompanied by a Resolution adopted by the City Council.
Honorable Mayor and City Council
October 1, 2024
Page 2
Fleet obtained a sole source documentation letter from Kalmikov Enterprises, Inc., dba Fire
Apparatus Solutions, Inc.
This matter was reviewed by Deputy City Attorney Ashleigh Stone on September 16, 2024,
Revenue Management Officer Geraldine Alejo on September 12, 2024, and by Purchasing
Agent Michelle Wilson on September 9, 2024.
SUSTAINABILITY
Maintenance of vehicles and equipment, including replacement of worn parts, ensures the fire
engines operate at peak efficiency, reducing downtime.
TIMING CONSIDERATIONS
City Council action to adopt a Resolution and award a contract concurrently is requested on
October 1, 2024, to ensure a new contract is in place expeditiously.
LEVINE ACT
This item is subject to the Levine Act. The Mayor, Councilmembers, and Commissioners who
have received a contribution of more than $250 within 12 months prior from a party, participant,
or their representatives involved in this proceeding may do either of the following: (1) disclose
the contribution on the record and recuse themselves from this proceeding; OR (2) return the
portion of the contribution that exceeds $250 within 30 days from the time the elected official
knew or should have known about the contribution and participate in the proceeding.
All parties, participants, and their representatives must disclose on the record of this proceeding
any contribution of more than $250 made to the Mayor or any Councilmembers within 12 months
prior to the date of the proceeding. The Mayor, Councilmembers, and Commissioners are
prohibited from accepting, soliciting, or directing a contribution of more than $250 from a party,
participant, or their representatives during a proceeding and for 12 months following the date a
final decision is rendered.
FISCAL IMPACT
The total annual contract amount will not exceed $220,000, inclusive of a 10 percent
contingency. An appropriation increase of $220,000 is requested in the Fleet Services Fund
Group in the Financial Management, offset by funds available generated by revenues received
from user departments. Parts and repair costs for fire engine trucks are charged to the General
Fund Group in the Fire Department as part of the Fleet Services MOU billing process. This
recommendation has no staffing impact beyond the normal budgeted scope of duties and is
consistent with existing City Council priorities. There is no local job impact associated with this
recommendation.

Subject: Comprehensive Ordinance for Enhanced Code Enforcement (Item 18)
-EXTERNAL-
District 5 Megan Kerr
I am writing this email in response to the Efforts by various members of the City Council in regards to
the potential to upgrade the current code enforcement (CE).
I have read the draft and agree with the points presented.
I would also like to add some items that will probably be addressed in greater detail down the line of
implementation wit specifics, but having this opportunity, will address.
First of all, I am a member of:
Bixby Highland Neighborhood Association
Bixby Highland Clean Streets
Ridgewood Triangle Clean Streets
Cal Hts Clean Streets
Los Cerritos Clean Streets
And i volunteer to clean in other City Council Districts when able. I am a "boots on the ground"
volunteer and i see concerns that need addressed with code enforcement enhancements. I would like
to break this down into areas that have been noted to be problematic and part of the CE.
1. Parking Enforcement
A. Parking on City Streets without current license plates or tags should be a priority as there are cars
taking up precious parking spaces that restrict street sweeping, and a haven for illegal activities
B. Implementation of no car camping ordinances (set up an area for this with toilets, monitoring,
handwashing, trash, support services)
C. Oversized vehicle enforcement parking to be a priority
2. Litter Abatement
A Vacant buildings and lots to be responsible to keep area clean and litter free routinely. Must
include steam claning of store fronts (currently used as toilet facilities!)
B. Trash and debris must be removed not blown into the street or bushes
C. Each business is responsible for providing a trash recepticle outside the business, and responsible
to dump daily.
D. Bike lanes also need more vigorous street cleaning by the City.
E. Cigarette/cigar butt receptacles to be available outside of eateries, laundromats, bars, etc
F. Add to GOLB app for section to remove signs put on telephone poles, lightpoles of unauthorized
marketing, i.e. "Cash fast for houses" or advertisements for events, etc.
Additionally, GOLB app is a great tool, and needs to have additional areas for reporting what is seen on
the streets, such as code violations!
Thank you!
Sherrie Dunn

April 18, 2024
Recommendation
Adopt Resolutions UT-1509 and UT-1510 authorizing the General Manager to execute
contracts, and any necessary subsequent amendments, with Measurement Control Systems
and Meter, Valve & Control, Inc., respectively, to furnish and deliver gas meters and other
services and parts, in an aggregate annual amount not to exceed $800,000 for a period of
one year, with the option to renew for two additional one-year periods.
Executive Summary
The Long Beach Utilities Department (LBUD) currently utilizes Honeywell Elster and Itron
natural gas meters at most large commercial and industrial customer accounts in Long Beach
and Signal Hill. These meters have a proven history of reliability and durability.
LBUD requests authorization to execute contracts with Measurement Control Systems (MCS)
and Meter, Valves and Control, Inc. (MVC) to purchase meters, regulators, and miscellaneous
parts and services to continue supporting Gas Services business operations. MCS is the
manufacturer-approved vendor for distribution of Honeywell Elster natural gas meters and
regulators, used by LBUD’s commercial customers; and MVC is the sole distributor of Itron
meter equipment, used by LBUD’s light-duty commercial and residential customers.
MCS and MVC have proven themselves to be reliable distributors of reliable products and
services. Given that the LBUD is federally regulated by the Department of Transportation’s
(DOT) Pipeline Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) and must comply with
all regulations, material specification, codes and standards in Code of Federal Regulations
(CRF) Title 49, Transportation, Part 192, it is important to continue using products and
services with a proven track record of safety, durability and reliability.
Fiscal Impact
The cost to the Gas Fund will be incurred in FY 24 – FY 25, with the total aggregate amount
not to exceed $800,000. These costs are included in the FY 24 budget and financial
projections.
Diana C. Tang Christopher J. Garner

RECOMMENDATION:
Recommendation to adopt a Resolution authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to
execute a contract and any necessary documents including any necessary subsequent
amendments, with Motorola Solutions, Inc., of Chicago, IL, for the purchase, delivery, and
implementation of an expanded 700 MHz Land Mobile Radio System inclusive of
communications equipment and services, in a total amount not to exceed $13,700,104,
for a period of two years, with the option to renew for four additional one-year periods, at
the discretion of the City Manager.
Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute a lease-purchase agreement and
related financing documents with Banc of America Public Capital Corp, of San Francisco,
CA, for the financing of 700 MHz Land Mobile Radio system, payable over a ten-year
period at an interest rate to be determined when the agreement is executed. (Citywide)
DISCUSSION
City Council approval is requested to enter into a contract with Motorola Solutions, Inc.
(Motorola), for the purchase, delivery, and implementation of an expanded 700 MHz Land Mobile
Radio system and the extended four-year warranty and support services, and to execute a lease-
purchase agreement through the City of Long Beach’s (City) Master Lease Agreement with Banc
of America Public Capital Corp (BAPCC), for the financing of the radio system.
Currently, the City’s Technology and Innovation Department (TID) operates mission-critical Land
Mobile Radio (LMR) systems for Police, Fire, Public Works, Disaster Preparedness, Habor,
Utilities, and Airport Departments on Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency
(UHF) systems and a limited 700 MHz system used minimally by Police and other City
Departments due to limited coverage and reliability. It is necessary to significantly expand our
current 700 MHz LMR system for the following reasons:
• to support enhanced user requirements,
• to mitigate challenges with aged radio equipment on VHF and UHF,
• to increase coverage both in-building and outdoors,
• to enhance the safety of our users and the public,
Honorable Mayor and City Council
January 16, 2024
Page 2
• to facilitate future regional interoperable communications, and
• to improve LMR system capabilities.
This project is essential for critical voice and data communications. It will enhance radio coverage
in the City, provide additional essential features, and enhance functionality, redundancy,
reliability, and resiliency of the existing 700 MHz LMR system for use by public safety and other
City Departments. With this expansion, the 700 MHz LMR system will become the City's primary
voice and data communications platform. It will facilitate future interoperability with other public
safety agencies in the County of Los Angeles and beyond which now use the 700 MHz spectrum
for LMR system communications.
Specifically, the expanded 700 MHz LMR system, as proposed by Motorola, will enhance the
primary transmit (TX) and receive (RX) radio site at Signal Hill and add three additional radio
sites at Dominguez Hills, Civic Center, and Reservoir Hill for coverage, reliability, and
redundancy. The upgraded system project includes doubling the number of available channels
from 14 to 28 for expanded user capabilities and capacity, replacing radio infrastructure at the
Signal Hill radio site, enhancing indoor coverage at strategic City facilities (to be determined)
with bi-directional amplifiers, assisting with creating a new fleet map/templates for the dispatch
radio consoles, providing assistance with reprogramming of dispatch consoles and radios with
the new radio template, enabling access to the 700 MHz LMR system by designated authorized
users through an iPhone application anywhere there is cell phone or Wifi service, supplying a
limited number of next-generation radios to select TID staff for performance testing for
prospective future user scenarios, providing training to TID staff, and comprehensive 24/7
support and maintenance by Motorola after system acceptance.
The legacy VHF and UHF LMR systems will remain operational for City Departments to use as
a backup to the expanded 700 MHz LMR system for tactical situational use, special operations,
and strategic scenarios as needed. This proposal leverages the existing 700 MHz LMR system
infrastructure where practical, including dispatch radio consoles and mobile and portable radios
(consistent with City Council approval of Motorola APX radio equipment in December 2018), for
significant cost savings and easier user adoption.
Motorola has agreed to offer the City the same terms and conditions as afforded to the County
of Los Angeles (L.A. County) in the Motorola/L.A. County master contract (L.A. County Master
Agreement) for a significant equipment discount of $800,869 and additional discounts for
infrastructure of $1,220,790, subscriber discount of $37,987 and Signal Hill radio site
improvement discount of $50,000. Motorola is offering $2,109,646 in discounts to the City, in
addition to the reduced pricing used in the L.A. County Master Agreement. The project's total
cost, including equipment, services, support and maintenance for four years including estimated
sales tax, is $13,700,104.
This purchase is proposed without a competitive bid process because the City’s existing
Motorola portable/mobile radios can be integrated seamlessly with the upgraded 700MHz
system. In addition, the City’s upgrade will allow for better interoperability with regional resources
and could play an essential role in the City’s timely response and recovery in a major disaster.
2
3
6
9
Honorable Mayor and City Council
January 16, 2024
Page 3
City Charter Section 1801 requires that contracts for City purchases be awarded to the lowest
responsible bidder after a competitive bid process, but allows for awards without a competitive
bid process when authorized by a Resolution adopted by the City Council.
City Council approval is also requested to authorize the City Manager to execute a ten-year
lease-purchase agreement through the City’s Master Lease Agreement with Banc of America
Public Capital Corp., to finance the LMR system. The Master Lease Agreement was approved
by the City Council on September 18, 2018, to provide lease financing for a variety of capital
equipment purchases. The Master Lease Agreement streamlines the purchasing and financing
process to provide a cost-effective approach to facilitate the purchase of essential capital assets.
This allows the City to meet immediate service demands for maintaining level annual
expenditures and spreading the acquisition costs over the term of the financing rather than
budgeting a large one-time capital project expenditure.
This matter was reviewed by Principal Deputy City Attorney Richard F. Anthony and Budget
Management Officer Nader Kaamoush on December 29, 2023, and by Purchasing Agent
Michelle Wilson on December 28, 2023.
TIMING CONSIDERATIONS
City Council action to adopt the Resolution and award a contract with Motorola concurrently, and
execute a lease-purchase agreement with Banc of America Public Capital Corp, is requested on
January 16, 2024, to ensure the contract is in place expeditiously.
LEVINE ACT
This item is subject to the Levine Act. The Mayor, Councilmembers, and Commissioners who
have received a contribution of more than $250 within 12 months prior from a party, participant,
or their representatives involved in this proceeding may do either of the following: (1) disclose
the contribution on the record and recuse themselves from this proceeding; OR (2) return the
portion of the contribution that exceeds $250 within 30 days from the time the elected official
knew or should have known about the contribution and participate in the proceeding.
All parties, participants, and their representatives must disclose on the record of this proceeding
any contribution of more than $250 made to the Mayor or any Councilmembers within 12 months
prior to the date of the proceeding. The Mayor, Councilmembers, and Commissioners are
prohibited from accepting, soliciting, or directing a contribution of more than $250 from a party,
participant, or their representatives during a proceeding and for 12 months following the date a
final decision is rendered.
FISCAL IMPACT
The total amount of the contract will not exceed $13,700,104. Based on the indicative interest
rate of 4.03 percent on December 15, 2023, the total amount for the lease purchase with Banc
of America Public Capital Corp is estimated at $16,668,277, which includes principal, interest,
and escrow fees. This equates to approximately $1,666,828 in annual debt service costs for the
10-year life of the financing. The amount is subject to change and will be finalized when the

agreement is executed. The lease purchase will be paid from the General Services Fund Group
in the Technology and Innovation Department. The annual debt service payments will be funded
by transfers from funds based on users of the system and is anticipated to be primarily funded
through Measure A in the General Fund Group. In Fiscal Year 2024 (FY 24), anticipated lease
cost is estimated to be $972,316. Any cost to Measure A in FY 24 will be absorbed within the
current Measure A plan using contingency set asides. Upon the execution of a final debt service
agreement, staff will return to City Council to request the necessary appropriation adjustments
for FY 24. The annual payments for FY 25 and beyond will be requested through the FY 25
budget development process and incorporated into the Measure A outyear plan. This
recommendation has no staffing impact beyond the normal budgeted scope of duties and is
consistent with the existing City Council priorities. There is no local job impact associated with
this recommendation.

14,000 pounds gross vehicle weight), including dump trucks, sewer vactor trucks, and
crane trucks. These mission-critical assets support water distribution and sewer collection
operations, and their availability is essential to maintaining safe, reliable utility services.
LBPUD conducted a competitive bid process under Specifications UD-26-313. Two bids
were received; however, only Los Angeles Truck Centers was determined to be
responsive and met all specification requirements. Despite receiving only one responsive
bid, staff determined the pricing to be fair and reasonable based on multiple objective
benchmarks. Parts pricing is tied to Mitchell UltraMate, a nationally recognized estimating
standard, ensuring pricing alignment with current published market rates. Labor rates are
consistent with prevailing regional market rates for heavy-duty vehicle repair services,
and the proposed markup for OEM parts falls within standard industry ranges. In addition,
the bid was compared to prior expenditures for similar services, reflecting typical market
adjustments. Collectively, these factors provide a reasonable basis to validate the
competitiveness of the bid.This contract will allow the Department to continue timely
maintenance and repair of specialized heavy-duty equipment, minimizing downtime and
ensuring continuity of operations.
This action supports the Department’s Business Plan by maintaining reliable and resilient
infrastructure and promoting operational efficiency.

Recommendation
Adopt Resolution No. UT-1520 authorizing the General
Manager to enter into a sole source agreement with Golden
Bell Products, Inc., for roach control services for sanitary
sewer manholes in the City of Long Beach, in an amount not
to exceed $200,900 for a one-year period, and to authorize
the General Manager to exercise the option to renew for two
additional one-year periods, subject to a maximum annual
increase of 6 percent.
